channel.title: planet — Essays on where systems tip
channel.description: planet – essays on tipping points, hysteresis and emergence in climate, politics, technology and markets. An offshoot of emergenz.art.

item.title: The vacancy
item.description: Is the failure in Antalya an opportunity? What Copenhagen teaches, what coalitions can do, and why consensus can only be abolished by consensus. A failure has no direction. On Copenhagen and Paris, the consensus rule, the Santa Marta coalition and the question of who fills the vacancy.

item.title: Overshoot is not a place
item.description: The final COP31 draft would have conceded that 1.5 degrees will be breached, and bet on the way back. Nothing was adopted. What hysteresis has to say about it. The temperature can come back; the climate that produced it cannot. On overshoot, hysteresis and the bet on carbon removal.

item.title: The bottleneck is in the wires
item.description: COP31 wanted electricity to supply a good third of our energy. The decision failed. Grids, copper and time were not ready anyway. A target can be agreed in one night; a transformer takes up to four years. On grids, copper and two systems running at different speeds.

item.title: The savings account
item.description: Glaciers, groundwater and a word that is changing its meaning. From water crisis to water bankruptcy: what glaciers and aquifers tell us about tipping points and hysteresis.

item.title: A cascade, not a cycle
item.description: Five recycling rates between 6 and 69 per cent, and the question behind the 15 per cent of Antalya. Plastic as an example: there are many recycling figures, but none that measures quality. A cycle loses nothing; a cascade loses something at every step.

item.title: Is something tipping here?
item.description: The slump in AI stocks after the 2026 US midterms, tested against the hallmarks of a tipping point. Sandpiles, reflexivity, coupled tipping points and hysteresis: what the post-election crash reveals about tipping points – and what it does not.

item.title: The threshold no one sees
item.description: An essay on artificial intelligence, emergence and the question of whether there is a tipping point. On abilities nobody programmed, jumps inside neural networks and the question of whether AGI is a tipping point.

item.title: Two clocks
item.description: An essay on climate policy, tipping points and responsibility for processes that outlast a legislative term. The political clock measures legislative terms, the climate clock centuries. On compromises physics does not recognise, and on responsibility.

item.title: No moment
item.description: A thesis on planetary cognition, the technosphere and the wrong question of the AGI debate. No neuron ever noticed that it had become part of a mind. Why asking for the day of AGI is the wrong question, and which future the technosphere anticipates.

item.title: The way back is a different one
item.description: An essay on hysteresis, attractors and the memory of complex systems. Why a system that has tipped does not return when the cause disappears – from clear lakes to ice sheets to societies.

item.title: The conveyor belt dies quietly
item.description: An essay on the AMOC, the physics of irreversibility and the failure of linear thinking. The Atlantic overturning circulation is weakening. Early warning signs, hysteresis, and a policy that dismantles its own instruments.
